# Command reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-command-docs.js from package.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every command is available from the Command Palette under the
**TIFF Visualizer** category. Many are also in the right-click menu inside an
open image.

| Command | ID | Keybinding |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Zoom Out | `tiffVisualizer.zoomOut` |  |

## Keybindings

These are active only while a Scientific Image Visualizer tab has focus, so
they do not shadow your normal editor bindings.

| Keybinding | Command |
| --- | --- |
| `ctrl` + `h` / `cmd` + `h (macOS)` | Toggle Histogram |
| `ctrl` + `m` / `cmd` + `m (macOS)` | Toggle Metadata Panel |
| `ctrl` + `shift` + `m` / `cmd` + `shift` + `m (macOS)` | Measure |
| `ctrl` + `shift` + `i` / `cmd` + `shift` + `i (macOS)` | Copy Image Information to Clipboard |

In **Open Image from URL**, `↑` / `↓` recall saved URLs in the input field;
the saved URLs are not displayed as a separate list.

Inside the image, `←` / `→` step through a dataset, collection or multi-page
TIFF, and `[` / `]` step through TIFF pages. Inside the measure panel, single
letters select tools — see [measurement](./measure.md).

## Settings

| Setting | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tiffVisualizer.navigationShortcuts` | `{}` |  |
| `tiffVisualizer.channels.autoComposite` | `false` | Open images whose channels are described by OME-TIFF or ImageJ metadata (fluorescence stacks, hyperstacks) in composite mode. Ordinary RGB images are not affected. Turning composite off by hand keeps it off for that preview. |
| `tiffVisualizer.channels.autoOpenPanel` | `false` | Open the Channels panel when an image whose channels are described by OME-TIFF or ImageJ metadata opens. For multi-page stacks it opens before the other channels have decoded, so the loading progress is visible. Applies once per file; ordinary RGB images are not affected. |
| `tiffVisualizer.channels.colorsByName` | `{}` | Channel tints by channel name, matched case-insensitively, for example {"DAPI": "#3399ff", "GFP": "#00ff00"}. Takes precedence over colorsByNumber and over colours stored in the file. |
| `tiffVisualizer.channels.colorsByNumber` | `{}` | Channel tints by channel number as shown in the Channels panel (starting at 1), for example {"1": "#00ff00"}. Takes precedence over colours stored in the file. |
| `tiffVisualizer.channels.groups` | `{}` | Named groups of channels for the Channels panel, for example {"T Cells": ["CD3e", "CD8", "CD4"]}. Each value lists channel names (exact, case-insensitive) or 1-based channel numbers. A group can be switched on or off, or soloed, as a unit. |
| `tiffVisualizer.cells.autoOpenPanel` | `"auto"` | When the Channels panel and its Cells section open by themselves. It opens once per file, so closing it is not undone as you step through Z or T. |
| `tiffVisualizer.cells.cellIdCol` | `[]` | Other names for the column that identifies the cell in a cell table (.parquet, .csv or .tsv), besides cell_id, for example ["Object"] for the intensity tables steinbock writes. Matched without regard to case; cell_id is tried first, then these in order. The ids must match the values painted in the mask image or the cell_id of the cell set the table is added to. |
| `tiffVisualizer.cells.cellData` | `{}` | Extra cell tables, as name → {path, parent}, for example {"xenium_segtraq": {"path": "segtraq/{sample_name}/{sample_name}.segtraq_cells.parquet", "parent": "Xenium cells"}}. Each file is a .parquet, .csv or .tsv table with a cell id column (cell_id, or a name from tiffVisualizer.cells.cellIdCol). It is listed under its parent cell set only, and its columns are merged into that set by cell id when you click Load. The parent is Xenium cells (the bundle's own cells) or a name from tiffVisualizer.cells.cellBoundaries. {sample_name} is the name of the folder that holds experiment.xenium in a Xenium bundle, and the image's file name without its extension (a.ome.tif gives a) in the image viewer. Relative paths start at the workspace folder. Used by the Xenium viewer and by the Cells section of the image viewer. Replaces tiffVisualizer.cells.cellsParquet, which is still read. |
| `tiffVisualizer.transcripts.groups` | `{}` | Gene groups for the Transcripts section of Xenium bundles, as name → gene list, for example {"Epithelial": ["EPCAM", "KRT8"]}, or name → {genes, color} to choose the group colour. Groups are offered in the Transcripts section's Add group list; none is added until you pick it. Groups can also be made in the panel, from a pasted list of gene names. |
| `tiffVisualizer.cells.cellBoundaries` | `{}` | Extra cell segmentations, as name → path, for example {"sam2": "sam2/{sample_name}/cell_boundaries.parquet", "cellpose": "masks/{sample_name}_mask.tif"}. Each file is a Xenium-style cell_boundaries.parquet (cell_id, vertex_x, vertex_y in microns), a .csv or .tsv of the same columns, or a .tif label mask (unsigned integers, objects numbered from 1). {sample_name} is the name of the folder that holds experiment.xenium in a Xenium bundle, and the image's file name without its extension (a.ome.tif gives a) in the image viewer. Relative paths start at the workspace folder. Used by the Xenium viewer and by the Cells section of the image viewer. Replaces tiffVisualizer.cells.cellBoundariesParquet, which is still read. Segmentations are listed in the Cells section and loaded when you click Load. |
| `tiffVisualizer.cells.nucleusBoundaries` | `{}` | Extra nucleus outlines, as name → {path, parent}, for example {"sam2_nuclei": {"path": "sam2/{sample_name}/nucleus_boundaries.parquet", "parent": "sam2"}}. Each file is a Xenium-style nucleus_boundaries.parquet (cell_id, vertex_x, vertex_y in microns) whose cell ids match its parent. It is listed under its parent cell set only and loaded when you click Load; a cell set shows one nucleus file at a time, so loading one replaces the previous. {sample_name} is the name of the folder that holds experiment.xenium in a Xenium bundle, and the image's file name without its extension (a.ome.tif gives a) in the image viewer. Relative paths start at the workspace folder. Replaces tiffVisualizer.cells.nucleusBoundariesParquet, which is still read. |
| `tiffVisualizer.gpuAcceleration` | `true` | Use GPU acceleration via WebGPU or WebGL2 for supported image rendering paths. Disable this if a GPU/driver causes incorrect output or slower rendering. |
| `tiffVisualizer.experimentalRegionDecode` | `false` | Experimental: use rectangle reads for images that have NO resolution pyramid, so the cost of a view follows the window rather than the file. Pyramidal images (Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF, whole-slide) do this already whenever their level is set to Auto, and are unaffected by this setting. Nothing uses it yet for images without a pyramid: drawing those a region at a time needs the canvas to become a window onto the image, which is not implemented. |

Display settings — normalization, gamma, brightness — are deliberately *not*
VS Code settings. They live for the lifetime of the window and reset when it
closes. See [rendering](./rendering.md).

## File associations

| Editor | Opens |
| --- | --- |
| Scientific Image Visualizer (`tiffVisualizer.previewEditor`) | `*.{tif,tiff,tf2,tf8,btf,exr,pfm,npy,npz,ppm,pgm,pbm,hdr,tga,rgb,rgba,sgi,bw,jxl,jxr,wdp,hdp,jp2,jpf,jpx,j2k,j2c,jpc,fits,fit,fts,dcm,dicom,DCM,DICOM,nc,cdf,czi,nd2,lif,sdt,ora,kra,psd,psb,xcf,afphoto,af}`, `*.{png,jpeg,jpg,bmp,ico,webp,avif}` |
| Xenium Viewer (`tiffVisualizer.xeniumViewer`) | `*.xenium` |

All supported formats use Scientific Image Visualizer by default, including
PNG/JPEG and Git revision previews. See
[formats](./formats.md).
